dedupe_keys.name: intrusion detection system for vehicular ad hoc network attacks based on machine learning techniques

description: The source establishes a multi-level machine-learning detector intended for vehicular ad-hoc network security. It combines random-forest and correlation-based feature selection with four tree-based classifiers and stacking. The reported evaluation uses CICIDS2017 and Python libraries; its high detection accuracy is bounded to that benchmark. This does not establish measured attacks on moving vehicles or operational real-time readiness, despite broader language in the abstract. The source authors provide the native description and file descriptors through Zenodo. Only metadata was inspected; no measurements, archives, source code or document bodies were retrieved. Public access and the deposit document licence do not establish executable access, software reuse rights or operating costs. Coverage remains bounded to the named experiments, with other geographic and temporal fields unknown. Related project resources may overlap; common project membership does not establish identical simulation inputs or results.
